chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umair, from Murazim ibn Hakim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
My father used to say: 'When you intend a good deed, hasten to do it, for you do not know what will occur.'
ai.seo_question: Why should one hasten to perform good deeds according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) conveys the wisdom of his father, Imam al-Baqir, emphasizing the urgency of acting on righteous intentions before unforeseen circumstances or death intervene. This teaching underscores the Shia concept of *fawq al-istidraj* (gradual entrapment) and the unpredictability of life, encouraging believers to seize the moment for worship and good deeds rather than procrastinating. It serves as a practical reminder that the opportunity for good is not guaranteed for tomorrow, aligning with the broader Islamic ethic of *ibda'* (initiation) in spiritual matters.
